hero.line: Above the city, a table worth the climb.
intro.paragraph: MIRADOR sits six floors above Damascus — one dining room, one long window, and a kitchen that answers to fire. We serve an international table: French technique, Mediterranean produce, no shortcuts. Below you, the city; above it, you.
acts.act1.title: I — Dusk
acts.act1.copy: The city switches on, window by window. From up here, its lights read as embers.
acts.act2.title: II — Fire
acts.act2.copy: In the kitchen, fire does the quiet work — a slow braise, a hissing plancha, patience.
acts.act3.title: III — The Table
acts.act3.copy: Six floors above the street, one table holds the whole skyline. Yours for the evening.

story.ch1.title: The Climb
story.ch1.body: There is no valet. There is a lift that takes its time, and a final flight of stairs where the noise of the street drops away with every step. By the last landing, the city is already below you — a field of small lights going about its evening. We chose the sixth floor for exactly this: the moment the doors open and the street turns into a view.
story.ch2.title: The Room
story.ch2.body: One room, forty seats, a single long window facing west. Materials are few and honest: darkened oak, brushed brass, linen. Light comes from low amber sources, as if the room itself were lit by the city below. Nothing on the walls — the skyline is the art.
story.ch3.title: The Evening
story.ch3.body: Service begins at six and ends when it ends. Courses leave the pass in their own order; the fire decides some of it. Ask for the ribeye for two and you will see why it needs the whole evening.
story.pullQuote: We kept only what the night required.
